test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 26 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: On 3rd October 2024, the Union Cabinet decided to merge all Central schemes in the agriculture sector into how many new schemes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Two**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• On 3rd October 2024, the Union Cabinet decided to merge all Central schemes in the agriculture sector into two new schemes.
 
• This decision aims to streamline and enhance the efficiency of the agricultural support provided by the government.
 
• The two new schemes are designed to cover various aspects of agricultural development, including input support, marketing, and infrastructure development.
 
• By merging the schemes, the government seeks to reduce redundancy and improve resource allocation within the agriculture sector.
 
• The merger is part of a broader strategy to boost agricultural productivity and ensure sustainable development in rural areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi (PM-KISAN)**

 
 
• PM-KISAN is a central sector scheme with 100% funding from the Government of India.
 
• Under the scheme, income support of Rs. 6,000 per year is provided to all landholding farmer families in three equal installments.
 
• This scheme aims to supplement the financial needs of farmers in procuring various inputs to ensure proper crop health and appropriate yields.
 
• The amount is directly transferred to the bank accounts of the beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)**
 
 
• Launched in 2016, PMFBY provides a comprehensive insurance cover against failure of the crop, thus helping in stabilizing the income of farmers.
 
• It aims to reduce the premium burden on farmers and ensure early settlement of crop insurance claims.
 
• The scheme covers all food & oilseed crops and annual commercial/horticultural crops for which past yield data is available.
 
• Farmers pay a nominal premium, and the remaining part of the actuarial premium is borne equally by the central and state governments.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)**
 
 
• PMKSY was launched with the vision to ensure access to some means of protective irrigation to all agricultural farms in the country.
 
• It aims to enhance the physical access of water on the farm and expand cultivable areas under assured irrigation.
 
• The scheme promotes precision irrigation technologies and practices.
 
• It integrates water source, distribution, and efficient farm-level application.
